steps.title: Buy the kit
hw: 4-DOF acrylic arm kit with MG90S servos, claw opening ≥ 75 mm
steps.note: Check the listed claw opening: it must be at least 75 mm for our 66 mm can
steps.how: Example: the ThinkRobotics 4-DOF acrylic arm (MG90S), listed with a 90 mm claw opening, 200 mm reach and 180 mm height (out of stock when checked). Many similar kits sell as "4DOF acrylic robot arm MG90S": pick one whose listing gives the claw opening. Avoid the 55 mm ones, which are too small for the can. Grey in the 3D view = the kit, drawn from those listed sizes, so yours will differ in detail.

steps.title: Build the kit as its manual says, except the claw
steps.note: Stop before fitting the claw onto the forearm
steps.how: Follow the kit's own manual: base, turntable, shoulder, both arm links. Don't fit the claw to the forearm yet: our wrist goes in between. That way nothing has to come apart later.

steps.title: Heavier footing
steps.how: The kit's 95 mm base would tip forward holding a can 127 mm out. Screw its base onto a plywood board with 4 wood screws through the kit's own base holes (you only drill wood), and add 2 washer stacks at the back.

steps.title: Insert our wrist roll
steps.note: Forearm → printed adapter → our MG90S → cross horn → printed adapter → kit claw
steps.how: This is the real modification: the kit has no wrist roll, and flipping the can needs one. 1) The wrist adapter slips between the forearm's 2 plates and is held by the same 2 screws that would have held the claw. 2) Our MG90S wrist servo goes through its window, 2 tab screws. 3) Cross horn on the claw adapter (4 servo-bag screws into printed pilots), wrist at 0°, press the horn onto the spline. 4) The kit's claw bolts onto the claw adapter with its own screws. No drilling into the acrylic.

steps.title: Pads for the can
hw: silicone or rubber strip 36 x 14 x 2 mm, x2
steps.how: Glue a silicone strip on each jaw where it meets the can. The flat acrylic jaws only touch a round can along a line; the pads spread the grip and stop it slipping while it flips.

steps.title: Wiring + software
steps.how: Five servos now: base turn, shoulder, elbow, claw (all from the kit) plus our wrist. The lift is no longer one servo: the shoulder and elbow move together to raise the can about 16 mm without tipping it. The firmware needs a new mapping (two angle pairs for LIFT, taught in the laptop panel); the sequence (grip, lift, flip, turn, lower, release) stays the same. Power 5 servos from a PCA9685 board on its own 5–6 V supply, not from the Uno. Not written yet: the 5-servo firmware.

report: CLAW OPENING: 90 mm listed vs can 66.2 + 2 x 2 mm pads = 70.2 -> PASS (20 mm to spare)
REACH: can centre 127 mm out vs 200 mm listed max reach -> PASS

SHOULDER (kit MG90S, 1.8 kg*cm): 59 g at the claw + the arm itself, x1.5 for moving -> 1.11 kg*cm = 61 % of stall -> MARGINAL: shoulder + elbow share it, move slowly (the kit's 4-bar puts part of it on the elbow servo)
TIP-OVER: kit base 95 mm wide alone would tip with a can at 127 mm; on the 180 x 155 board with 2 x 70 g washers -> PASS
FLIP: our MG90S turns the claw 180 deg about the forearm axis (the kit has no wrist roll: this is the main change)
